problem: Let $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x+y).$ Find the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,1).$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Best Linear Approximation of a Multivariable Function
examples.problem: Let $f(x,y, z)= xyz+y^2.$ Find the best linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3, -1, 1).$
examples.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z) \approx f(a,b,c) + \nabla f(a,b,c)\cdot \langle x-a, y-b, z-c \rangle.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3, -1, 1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(3,-1,1)+∇f(3,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x-3,y+1,z-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the definition of $f,$ we have that $f(3, -1, 1)= -2.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x} & =yz\, &  & ⇒\, &  & {f}_{x}(3,-1,1)=-1, \\ {f}_{y} & =xz+2y\, &  & ⇒\, &  & {f}_{y}(3,-1,1)=1 \\ {f}_{z} & =xy\, &  & ⇒\, &  & {f}_{z}(3,-1,1)=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient of the function at the point $(3, -1,1)$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(3,-1,1) & =⟨-1,1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the linear approximation of the function $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(3,-1,1)+∇f(3,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x-3,y+1,z-1⟩ \\  & =-2+⟨-1,1,-3⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y+1,z-1⟩ \\  & =-2-(x-3)+(y+1)-3(z-1) \\  & =-2-x+3+y+1-3z+3 \\  & =5-x+y-3z.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y,z)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(-1,1,0)=-1,\,{f}_{x}(-1,1,0)=1,\,{f}_{y}(-1,1,0)=-2,\,{f}_{z}(-1,1,0)=0.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,1,0)$ estimate the value of $f(-1,1.01,-0.01)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,1,0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(-1,1,0)+∇f(-1,1,0)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),y-1,z-0⟩ \\  & =f(-1,1,0)+⟨{f}_{x}(-1,1,0),{f}_{y}(-1,1,0),{f}_{z}(-1,1,0)⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y-1,z⟩ \\  & =-1+⟨1,-2,0⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y-1,z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-1,1.01,-0.01)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=-1,$ $y=1.01,$ and $z=-0.01$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1,1.01,-0.01) & ≈-1+⟨1,-2,0⟩\cdot ⟨-1+1,1.01-1,-0.01⟩ \\  & =-1+⟨1,-2,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,0.01,-0.01⟩ \\  & =-1+1(0)-2(0.01)+0(-0.01) \\  & =-1+0-0.02+0 \\  & =-1.02\end{aligned}
$$
